en: Mount Mayon in the Philippines is famous for its perfectly symmetrical cone shape and frequent explosive eruptions.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park features an eight-kilometer underground river that flows directly into the sea.
Tugtupite is a rare, fluorescent pink mineral found almost exclusively on Sibaltan Island in Palawan, Philippines.
Olympus Mons on Mars is the tallest known volcano in the solar system, standing about three times higher than Mount Everest.
Typhoon Rolly, known internationally as Goni, made landfall in the Philippines in 2020 as one of the strongest tropical cyclones ever recorded.
The Apollo 11 astronauts landed their lunar module in the Mare Tranquillitatis, also known as the Sea of Tranquility.
Sirius, located in the constellation Canis Major, is the brightest star visible in the Earth's night sky.
The volcanic ash from the 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo eventually weathered into highly fertile andisols for local farmers.
The municipality of General Santos in Mindanao experiences a tropical savanna climate with a distinct dry season from November to April.
Ceres is the only dwarf planet located in the inner solar system, orbiting within the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol are made of thousands of symmetrical limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
The Angat Watershed Forest Reserve in Bulacan captures heavy monsoon rainfall, which recharges the Angat Dam that supplies water to Metro Manila.
